title: Routing repetition rate
goal:
Table 5 of the paper reports how often a token and the next token in the same text get the same expert (Section 5). Write `repeat_rates(idx)`.

`idx` has shape `(T, 2)`: for each of `T` consecutive tokens, the two experts chosen, with the first choice in column 0. Return a pair `(first, either)`:

- `first`: the fraction of the `T - 1` consecutive pairs whose first choices are equal.
- `either`: the fraction of consecutive pairs whose chosen sets share at least one expert, in any slot.

With 8 experts and random routing, the expected values are $1/8 = 12.5\%$ and $1 - (6/8)(5/7) \approx 46.4\%$. The paper doesn't define the second column of Table 5 beyond "the same expert is observed as first or second choice"; this exercise uses the set-overlap reading, because it reproduces the paper's 46% baseline.
hints: For `either`, compare each of the two experts of token $t+1$ with each of the two experts of token $t$. A broadcast `idx[1:, :, None] == idx[:-1, None, :]` has shape `(T-1, 2, 2)`.
Reduce the `(T-1, 2, 2)` array with `.any(axis=(1, 2))` before you take the mean. Counting the matches instead of testing for any match gives a number above 1 in some pairs.
